title: The summer a whole city couldn't stop dancing 💃
subject: dance
description:
What do you think really caused it? 👇

In July 1518, the dancing plague swept Strasbourg. Here's what the records show, what the city did about it, and the leading theory on why it happened.

Sources: John Waller, The Lancet (2009), The Public Domain Review (Ned Pennant-Rea), HistoryNet

scenes.text: In 1518, a woman started dancing and couldn't stop.
There was no music. Within a week, about 30 people had joined Frau Troffea in Strasbourg.
By August, estimates range from 50 to 400 dancers.
But here's the strange part. The city's cure was more dancing, in guild halls, with hired musicians.
It backfired. Music was banned, and the dancers were sent to Saint Vitus's shrine in red shoes.
Historian John Waller blames mass psychogenic illness, fueled by famine. Still, no one can prove why,
